name: Media — netflix_wikipedia_pageviews covariate forecasting bundle (daily)
citation: Wikimedia Pageviews REST API; Yahoo Finance (yfinance)
license: Wikimedia pageviews: CC0 1.0 Public Domain; Yahoo Finance data for research use.
description: Non-EIA, non-benchmark web-attention + equity data. Pageviews use agent=user (bots stripped) so the stored series is not bot-inflated; no all-agents series and no user-vs-all duplicate of any target are included (avoids leakage). These sources are not standard forecasting-benchmark training corpora. Long-format TempusBench bundle for application 'covariate_media_daily_streaming_attention'. Target 'netflix_wikipedia_pageviews' forecast from 4 covariates. daily cadence, 3018 timesteps, 2018-04-03..2026-07-07. NON-EIA (the foundation model is EIA-trained, so EIA sources are excluded). eia_derived=false.
preprocessing: 1. Pull Wikimedia daily pageviews (agent=user) for Netflix, Stranger_Things, Spotify from 20160101 to 20260707 via REST with User-Agent header; cache raw JSON.
2. Pull yfinance NFLX and SPOT daily Close (auto_adjust=True) from 2016-01-01 to end; cache raw CSV.
3. Compute first-available date per source; set common-overlap start = latest first date (SPOT IPO 2018-04-03); end = today - 7 days.
4. Build a continuous daily calendar index over the common span.
5. Reindex pageviews onto the calendar; linear-interpolate internal gaps of <=3 consecutive days.
6. Forward-fill equity closes across weekends/holidays onto the calendar.
7. Derive deterministic known-future calendar covariates: dow, is_weekend, is_holiday (USFederalHolidayCalendar).
8. Order columns date, targets, covariates; interpolate/ffill/bfill any residual NaN so the final CSV has zero NaN; write CSV + meta.json.
9. Reformatted wide->long TempusBench (variable_name, variable_unit, timestamps, values); timestamps ISO-8601 UTC; variable names expanded; missing->null; values round-trip-verified against source.

10. Removed the day_of_week calendar covariate. Retained two binary calendar flags — 'is weekend' and 'is holiday' (0/1, both derivable from the shared 'timestamps') — as covariates, since they are genuine drivers (e.g. 'is weekend' was the selected winning covariate for the Netflix-attention forecast).

11. Variable names are written in plain English (underscores replaced with spaces). Target — 'netflix wikipedia pageviews' (from source column 'netflix_views', unit: views/day). Covariates — 'stranger things wikipedia pageviews' (from 'stranger_things_views', views/day); 'spotify wikipedia pageviews' (from 'spotify_views', views/day); 'netflix share price' (from 'nflx_close', USD); 'spotify share price' (from 'spot_close', USD); 'is weekend' (from 'is_weekend', binary 0/1); 'is holiday' (from 'is_holiday', binary 0/1).
12. Removed the calendar covariates 'is weekend' and 'is holiday' from the delivered CSV.
